Index discipulorum
Περὶ τῶν οʹ ἀποστόλων.
αʹ. Ἰάκωβος ὁ ἀδελφὸς τοῦ κυρίου τὸ κατὰ σάρκα, ὁ καὶ ἐπικληθεὶς δίκαιος
καὶ πρῶτος ἐπίσκοπος Ἱεροσολύμων χειροτονηθείς, λίθοις βληθεὶς ὑπὸ τῶν
Ἰουδαίων ἐν αὐτῇ τῇ Ἱερουσαλὴμ ἐκοιμήθη καὶ ἐκεῖ ἐτάφη ἐν τῷ ναῷ πλησίον τῶν
ἱερέων.
βʹ. Τιμόθεος ὁ ὑπὸ Παύλου ἐπίσκοπος γενόμενος Ἐφέσου ἐν τῷ Ἰλλυρικῷ καὶ
ἐν ἁπάσῃ τῇ Ἑλλάδι ἀρξάμενος ἀπὸ Ἐφέσου, ἐκήρυξε τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τοῦ κυρίου
Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ· ἐκεῖ οὖν ἀπέθανε καὶ ἐκεῖ ἐτάφη ἐνδόξως.
γʹ. Τίτος ὁ ἐπίσκοπος Κρήτης αὐτῇ τῇ Κρήτῃ, ταῖς τε πέριξ νήσοις ἐκήρυξε τὸ
εὐαγγέλιον τοῦ Χριστοῦ, κἀκεῖσε ἀποθανὼν ἐτάφη ἐνδόξως.
δʹ. Βαρνάβας ὁ μετὰ Παύλου τῷ λόγῳ διακονήσας πρῶτος ἐν Ῥώμῃ τὸν
Χριστὸν ἐκήρυξε· μετέπειτα δὲ Μεδιολάνων ἐπίσκοπος ἐγένετο.
εʹ. Ἀνανίας ὁ βαπτίσας τὸν ἅγιον Παῦλον ∆αμασκοῦ ἐπίσκοπος ἐγένετο.
ς ʹ. Στέφανος ὁ πρωτομάρτυς, ὁ εἷς τῶν ἑπτὰ διακόνων, λιθοβληθεὶς
ἐτελειώθη ὑπὸ τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἐν Ἱερουσαλήμ, ὡς Λουκᾶς μαρτυρεῖ ἐν ταῖς πράξεσι
τῶν ἀποστόλων.
119 ζʹ. Φίλιππος ὁ καὶ αὐτὸς εἷς τῶν ἑπτά, ὁ καὶ Σίμωνα καὶ τὸν εὐνοῦχον
βαπτίσας ἐν Τράλλεσι τῆς Ἀσίας ἐπίσκοπος γέγονεν.
ηʹ. Πρόχωρος ὁ καὶ αὐτὸς εἷς τῶν ἑπτά, Νικομηδείας τῆς κατὰ Βιθυνίαν
ἐπίσκοπος γέγονεν.
θʹ. Νικάνωρ ὁ καὶ αὐτὸς εἷς τῶν ἑπτά, κατ' αὐτὴν τὴν ἡμέραν καὶ αὐτὸς τὸν
βίον ἐξετέλεσε, καθ' ἣν καὶ ὁ συνδιάκονος αὐτοῦ καὶ πρωτομάρτυς Στέφανος σὺν
δισχιλίοις ἄλλοις τῶν ἠλπικότων εἰς Χριστόν.
ιʹ. Σίμων ὁ καὶ αὐτὸς εἷς τῶν ἑπτά, ὁ καὶ ἐπίσκοπος Βόστρων Ἀράβων
γενόμενος· ἐκαύθη ὑπὸ τῶν Ἑλλήνων.
ιαʹ. Παρμενᾶς ὁ καὶ αὐτὸς εἷς τῶν ἑπτά, οὗτος ἐπ' ὄψεσι τῶν ἀποστόλων
ἀπέθανεν ἐν τῇ διακονίᾳ αὐτοῦ.
ιβʹ. Νικόλαος ὁ καὶ αὐτὸς εἷς τῶν ἑπτά, οὗτος γέγονε μὲν Σαμαρείας
ἐπίσκοπος· ἑτεροδοξήσας δὲ ἅμα τῷ Σίμωνι ἀπέστη.
ιγʹ. Κλεόπας ὁ καὶ Συμεὼν ὁ ἀνέψιος τοῦ κυρίου, ὃς καὶ εἶδεν αὐτὸν καὶ
ὡμίλησεν ἅμα καὶ τῷ Λουκᾷ συνοδεύσας μετὰ τὸ ἀναστῆναι τοῦτον ἐκ τῶν νεκρῶν,
ὡς ἐν τῷ 120 εὐαγγελίῳ γέγραπται· οὗτος ἐπίσκοπος Ἱεροσολύμων ἐγένετο
δεύτερος.
ιδʹ. Σίλας ὁ μετὰ Παύλου τῷ λόγῳ διακονήσας ἐν Κορίνθῳ ἐπίσκοπος
γέγονεν.
ιεʹ. Κρήσκης, οὗ μέμνηται ὁ ἀπόστολος Παῦλος ἐν τῇ πρὸς Τιμόθεον δευτέρᾳ
ἐπιστολῇ, ὁ καὶ ἐπίσκοπος Χαλκηδόνος τῶν ἐν Γαλλίαις γενόμενος ἐκεῖ ἐκήρυξε τὸ
εὐαγγέλιον τοῦ Χριστοῦ· ἐπὶ δὲ Τραιανοῦ βασιλέως καὶ ἐμαρτύρησε καὶ ἐτάφη ἐκεῖ.
ις ʹ. Ἐπαινετός, οὗ ὁ ἀπόστολος μέμνηται ἐν τῇ πρὸς Ῥωμαίους ἐπιστολῇ,
ἐπίσκοπος Καρθαγένης ἐγένετο.
ιζʹ. Ἀνδρόνικος, οὗ καὶ αὐτοῦ ὁ ἀπόστολος Παῦλος ἐν τῇ πρὸς Ῥωμαίους
ἐπιστολῇ μέμνηται, ἐπίσκοπος Παννονίας ἐγένετο. ιηʹ. Ἀμπλίας, οὗ καὶ αὐτοῦ
μέμνηται ὁ Παῦλος ἐν τῇ πρὸς Ῥωμαίους ἐπιστολῇ, ἐπίσκοπος Ὀδύσσου ἐγένετο.
ιθʹ. Οὐρβανός, οὗ καὶ αὐτοῦ μέμνηται ὁ Παῦλος ἐν τῇ πρὸς Ῥωμαίους
english: Concerning the seventy apostles. 1. James, the brother of the Lord according to the flesh, who was also called the Just, became the first bishop of Jerusalem; having been stoned by the Jews in that same Jerusalem, he fell asleep and was buried there in the temple near the shrines. 2. Timothy, who became bishop under Paul in Ephesus, beginning in Illyricum and throughout all of Greece, preached the gospel of the Lord Jesus Christ; there, therefore, he died and was gloriously buried. 3. Titus, the bishop of Crete, preached the gospel of Christ to Crete and its surrounding islands, and having died there, he was gloriously buried. 4. Barnabas, who first ministered the word with Paul in Rome, later became bishop of Mediolanum. 5. Ananias, who baptized the holy Paul, became bishop of Damascus. 6. Stephen, the first martyr and one of the seven deacons, was completed by stoning by the Jews in Jerusalem, as Luke testifies in the Acts of the Apostles. 7. Philip, who was also one of the seven, and who baptized Simon and the eunuch, became bishop of Tralles in Asia. 8. Prochorus, who was also one of the seven, became bishop of Nicomedia in Bithynia. 9. Nicanor, who was also one of the seven, completed his life on that very same day on which his fellow deacon and first martyr Stephen, along with thousands of others who had hoped in Christ, [was martyred]. 10. Simon, who was also one of the seven, became bishop of Bostra in Arabia; he was burned by the Greeks. 11. Parmenas, who was also one of the seven, died in his ministry in the sight of the apostles. 12. Nicholas, who was also one of the seven, became bishop of Samaria, but having fallen into heresy, he departed along with Simon. 13. Cleopas and Simeon, the cousin of the Lord, who saw Him and spoke with Him, and who also accompanied Luke after this one rose from the dead, as is written in the Gospel; this one became the second bishop of Jerusalem. 14. Silas, who ministered the word with Paul, became bishop of Corinth. 15. Crescas, whom the apostle Paul mentions in the second epistle to Timothy, became bishop of Chalcedon in Gaul, where he preached the gospel of Christ; he also bore witness and was buried there during the reign of Emperor Trajan. 16. Epaenetus, whom the apostle mentions in the epistle to the Romans, became bishop of Carthage. 17. Andronicus, whom the apostle Paul also mentions in the epistle to the Romans, became bishop of Pannonia. 18. Ampliatus, whom Paul also mentions in the epistle to the Romans, became bishop of Odysseus. 19. Urbanus, whom Paul also mentions in the epistle to the Romans...

ἐπιστολῇ, ἐπίσκοπος Μακεδονίας ἐγένετο.
κʹ. Στάχυς, οὗ καὶ αὐτοῦ ἐν τῇ αὐτῇ ἐπιστολῇ μέμνηται ὁ Παῦλος, ἐπίσκοπος
πρῶτος Βυζαντίου κατέστη ὑπὸ Ἀνδρέου τοῦ ἀποστόλου ἐν Ἀργυροπόλει τῆς
Θρᾴκης.
καʹ. Ἀπελλῆς, οὗ καὶ αὐτοῦ ἐν τῇ αὐτῇ ἐπιστολῇ ὁ 121 Παῦλος μέμνηται,
ἐπίσκοπος Σμύρνης ἐγένετο πρὸ τοῦ ἁγίου Πολυκάρπου.
κβʹ. Ἀριστόβουλος, οὗ καὶ αὐτοῦ ἐν τῇ αὐτῇ ἐπιστολῇ ὁ Παῦλος μέμνηται,
ἐπίσκοπος Βρεττανίας ἐγένετο.
κγʹ. Νάρκισσος, οὗ καὶ αὐτοῦ ἐν τῇ αὐτῇ ἐπιστολῇ ὁ αὐτὸς μέμνηται,
ἐπίσκοπος Ἀθηνῶν ἐγένετο.
κδʹ. Ἡρωδίων, οὗ καὶ αὐτοῦ ἐν τῇ αὐτῇ ἐπιστολῇ ὁ αὐτὸς μέμνηται,
ἐπίσκοπος Πατρῶν ἐγένετο. κεʹ. Ῥοῦφος, οὗ καὶ αὐτοῦ ἐν τῇ αὐτῇ ἐπιστολῇ ὁ αὐτὸς
μέμνηται, ἐπίσκοπος Θηβῶν ἐγένετο.
κς ʹ. Ἀσύγκριτος, οὗ καὶ αὐτοῦ ἐν τῇ αὐτῇ ἐπιστολῇ ὁ αὐτὸς μέμνηται,
ἐπίσκοπος Ὑρκανίας γέγονεν.
κζʹ. Φλέγων, οὗ καὶ αὐτοῦ ἐν τῇ αὐτῇ ἐπιστολῇ ὁ αὐτὸς μέμνηται, ἐπίσκοπος
Μαραθῶνος γέγονεν.
κηʹ. Ἑρμῆς, οὗ καὶ αὑτοῦ ἐν τῇ αὐτῇ ἐπιστολῇ ὁ αὐτὸς μέμνηται ἀπόστολος,
ἐπίσκοπος ∆αλματίας ἐγένετο.
κθʹ. Ἑρμᾶς, οὗ καὶ αὐτοῦ ἐν τῇ αὐτῇ ἐπιστολῇ ὁ αὐτὸς μέμνηται ἀπόστολος,
ἐπίσκοπος Φιλίππων πόλεως ἐγένετο.
122 λʹ. Πατρόβας, οὗ καὶ αὐτοῦ ὁ αὐτὸς ἀπόστολος Παῦλος μέμνηται,
ἐπίσκοπος ἐν Νε Ποτιόλοις ἐγένετο.
λαʹ. Ἄγαβος, ὁ ἐν ταῖς πράξεσι τῶν ἀποστόλων μνημονευόμενος, οὗτος καὶ
προφητικοῦ ἠξιώθη χαρίσματος.
λβʹ. Λῖνος, οὗ καὶ αὐτοῦ ὁ ἀπόστολος Παῦλος μέμνηται, πρῶτος ἐπίσκοπος
Ῥώμης μετὰ Πέτρον τὸν κορυφαῖον ἐγένετο.
λγʹ. Γάϊος, οὗ καὶ αὐτοῦ ὁ ἀπόστολος Παῦλος μέμνηται, ἐπίσκοπος Ἐφέσου
μετὰ Τιμόθεον γέγονεν.
λδʹ. Φιλόλογος, οὗ καὶ αὐτοῦ ὁ Παῦλος μέμνηται, ἐπίσκοπος Σινώπης ὑπὸ
Ἀνδρέου ἐγένετο.
λεʹ. Ὀλυμπᾶς, οὗ καὶ αὐτοῦ ὁ Παῦλος μέμνηται, οὗτος ἐν Ῥώμῃ ἅμα Πέτρῳ
τῷ κορυφαίῳ ἐμαρτύρησε τὴν κεφαλὴν ἀποτμηθείς.
λ ςʹ. Ῥωδίων, οὗ καὶ αὐτοῦ ὁ Παῦλος μέμνηται, καὶ αὐτὸς ὁμοίως ἐν Ῥώμῃ
μετὰ Πέτρου καὶ Ὀλυμπᾶ τῷ μαρτυρίῳ ἐτελειώθη τὴν κεφαλὴν καὶ αὐτὸς
ἀποτμηθείς.
ληʹ. Ἰάσων, οὗ καὶ αὐτοῦ ὁ Παῦλος μέμνηται, ἐπίσκοπος Ταρσοῦ ἐγένετο. 123
λθʹ. Σωσίπατρος, οὗ καὶ αὐτοῦ ὁμοίως ὁ Παῦλος μέμνηται, ἐπίσκοπος Ἰκονίου
ἐγένετο.
μʹ. Λούκιος, οὗ καὶ αὐτοῦ ὁ Παῦλος μέμνηται, ἐπίσκοπος ἐν Λαοδικείᾳ τῆς
Συρίας ἐγένετο.
μαʹ. Τέρτιος ὁ κατ' αὐτὴν τὴν πρὸς Ῥωμαίους ἐπιστολὴν τοῦ Παύλου γράψας
english: ...in the epistle, he became bishop of Macedonia. 33. Stachys, whom Paul also mentions in the same epistle, became the first bishop of Byzantium in Argyropolis of Thrace under Andrew the apostle. 34. Apelles, whom Paul also mentions in the same epistle, became bishop of Smyrna before Saint Polycarp. 36. Aristobulus, whom Paul also mentions in the same epistle, became bishop of Britain. 37. Narcissus, whom the same Paul also mentions in the same epistle, became bishop of Athens. 38. Herodion, whom the same Paul also mentions in the same epistle, became bishop of Patras. 40. Rufus, whom the same Paul also mentions in the same epistle, became bishop of Thebes. 46. Asyncritus, whom the same Paul also mentions in the same epistle, became bishop of Hyrcania. 47. Phlegon, whom the same Paul also mentions in the same epistle, became bishop of Marathon. 48. Hermes, whom the same Paul also mentions in the same epistle as an apostle, became bishop of Dalmatia. 49. Hermas, whom the same Paul also mentions in the same epistle as an apostle, became bishop of the city of Philippi. 50. Ptrobas, whom the same apostle Paul also mentions, became bishop in Neopotamos. 51. Agabus, who is mentioned in the Acts of the Apostles, who was also worthy of the gift of prophecy. 52. Linus, whom the apostle Paul also mentions, became the first bishop of Rome after Peter the chief. 53. Gaius, whom the apostle Paul also mentions, became bishop of Ephesus after Timothy. 54. Philologus, whom Paul also mentions, became bishop of Sinope under Andrew. 55. Olympus, whom Paul also mentions, who in Rome, together with Peter the chief, bore witness by having his head cut off. 56. Rhodian, whom Paul also mentions, who likewise in Rome, together with Peter and Olympus, completed his witness by having his head cut off. 57. Jason, whom Paul also mentions, became bishop of Tarsus. 58. Sosipater, whom Paul also mentions in the same way, became bishop of Iconium. 59. Lucius, whom Paul also mentions, became bishop in Laodicea of Syria. 61. Tertius, who wrote the epistle to the Romans by Paul.

ἐπίσκοπος δεύτερος Ἰκονίου ἐγένετο.
μβʹ. Ἔραστος, οὗ καὶ αὐτοῦ μέμνηται Παῦλος ἐν τῇ αὐτῇ ἐπιστολῇ, οἰκονόμος
τῆς ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις ἐκκλησίας ἐγένετο, ἔπειτα ἐπίσκοπος Πανεάδος ἐγένετο.
μγʹ. Φύγελος, οὗ καὶ αὐτοῦ ὁ Παῦλος μέμνηται ὡς ἑτεροδοξήσαντος καὶ τὰ
Σίμωνος φρονήσαντος, ἐπίσκοπος Ἐφέσου γέγονεν.
μδʹ. Ἑρμογένης, οὗ καὶ αὐτοῦ ὁ Παῦλος ὁμοίως ὡς ἑτεροδοξήσαντος
μέμνηται, ἐπίσκοπος ἐν Μεγάροις ἐγένετο.

μεʹ. ∆ημᾶς, οὗ καὶ αὐτοῦ ὁμοίως ὁ ἀπόστολος Παῦλος μέμνηται ὡς
ἀποστήσαντος· δηλοῖ γὰρ περὶ τῶν τριῶν ἐν τῇ πρὸς Τιμόθεον δευτέρᾳ αὐτοῦ
ἐπιστολῇ, ὅτι ἑτεροδοξήσαντες Φύγελος καὶ Ἑρμογένης ἀντέστησαν τῇ διδασκαλίᾳ
αὐτοῦ. Ὁ δὲ ∆ημᾶς ἀγαπήσας τὸν νῦν αἰῶνα κατέλιπε τὸν εὐαγγελικὸν λόγον, καὶ ἐν
Θεσσαλονίκῃ ἱερεὺς τῶν εἰδώλων ἐγένετο. Περὶ τούτων καὶ Ἰωάννης ὁ ἀπόστολος
ἔγραψεν· ἐξ ἡμῶν ἐξῆλθον, ἀλλ' οὐκ ἦσαν ἐξ ἡμῶν.
μς ʹ. Κούαρτος, οὗ καὶ αὐτοῦ ἐν τῇ πρὸς Ῥωμαίους ἐπιστολῇ ὁ Παῦλος
μέμνηται, ἐπίσκοπος Βηρυτοῦ ἐγένετο.
124 μζʹ. Ἀπολλώς, οὗ καὶ αὐτοῦ ἐν τῇ πρὸς Κορινθίους ἐπιστολῇ ὁ Παῦλος
μέμνηται, ἐπίσκοπος Καισαρείας ἐγένετο.
μηʹ. Κηφᾶς, ὃν ὁ ἀπόστολος Παῦλος ἐν Ἀντιοχείᾳ ἤλεγξε διαλεχθεὶς
ὁμωνυμοῦντα τῷ Πέτρῳ, ἐπίσκοπος Κονίας ἐγένετο.
μθʹ. Σωσθένης, οὗ καὶ αὐτοῦ ὁ Παῦλος μέμνηται, ἐπίσκοπος Κολοφονιάδος
ἐγένετο.
νʹ. Ἐπαφρόδιτος, οὗ καὶ αὐτοῦ ὁ Παῦλος μέμνηται, ἐπίσκοπος Ἀδριακῆς
ἐγένετο. ναʹ. Καῖσαρ, οὗ καὶ αὐτοῦ ὁ Παῦλος μέμνηται, ἐπίσκοπος ∆υῤῥαχίου
ἐγένετο.
νβʹ. Μάρκος ὁ ἀνέψιος Βαρνάβα, οὗ καὶ ὁ Παῦλος μέμνηται, ἐπίσκοπος
Ἀπολλωνιάδος ἐγένετο.
νγʹ. Ἰωσὴφ ὁ λεγόμενος καὶ Ἰοῦστος καὶ Βαρσαββᾶς, οὗ μέμνηται Λουκᾶς ἐν
ταῖς πράξεσι τῶν ἀποστόλων ὡς συγκληρωθέντος τῷ Ματθίᾳ, ἐπίσκοπος
Ἐλευθεροπόλεως γέγονε.
νδʹ. Ἀρτεμᾶς, οὗ καὶ αὐτοῦ ὁ Παῦλος μέμνηται, ἐπίσκοπος ἐν Λύστρᾳ
ἐγένετο.
νεʹ. Κλήμης, οὗ καὶ αὐτοῦ ὁ Παῦλος μέμνηται, λέγων· μετὰ Κλήμεντος καὶ
τῶν λοιπῶν συνεγρῶν μου, ὃς καὶ πρῶ125 τος ἐξ ἐθνῶν καὶ Ἑλλήνων ἐπίστευσεν εἰς
Χριστόν, ἐπίσκοπος Σαρδικῆς ἐγένετο.
νς ʹ. Ὀνησίφορος, οὗ καὶ αὐτοῦ ὁ Παῦλος μέμνηται, ἐπίσκοπος Κορωνείας
ἐγένετο.
νζʹ. Τυχικός, οὗ καὶ αὐτοῦ μέμνηται ὁ Παῦλος, πρῶτος ἐπίσκοπος
Χαλκηδόνος τῆς ἐν Βιθυνίᾳ ἐγένετο.
νηʹ. Κάρπος, οὗ καὶ αὐτοῦ ὁ Παῦλος μέμνηται, ἐπίσκοπος Βεῤῥοίας τῆς
Θρᾴκης ἐγένετο. νθʹ. Εὔοδος, οὗ καὶ αὐτοῦ ὁ Παῦλος μέμνηται, πρῶτος ἐπίσκοπος
english: He became the second bishop of Iconium. 42. Erastus, whom Paul also mentions in the same epistle, became the steward of the church in Jerusalem, and later became the bishop of Paneas. 43. Phygellus, whom Paul also mentions as having departed from the faith, and likewise Simon, became the bishop of Ephesus. 44. Hermogenes, whom Paul also similarly mentions as having departed from the faith, became the bishop in Megara. 45. Demas, whom the apostle Paul also similarly mentions as having deserted; for he speaks concerning these three in his second epistle to Timothy, that Phygellus and Hermogenes, having departed from the faith, opposed his teaching. But Demas, having loved this present age, abandoned the gospel word, and became a priest of idols in Thessalonica. Concerning these, the apostle John also wrote: 'They went out from us, but they were not of us.' 46. Quartus, whom Paul also mentions in the epistle to the Romans, became the bishop of Beirut. 124. 47. Apollos, whom Paul also mentions in the epistle to the Corinthians, became the bishop of Caesarea. 48. Cephas, whom the apostle Paul rebuked in Antioch for acting in agreement with Peter, became the bishop of Konya. 49. Sosthenes, whom Paul also mentions, became the bishop of Colossae. 50. Epaphroditus, whom Paul also mentions, became the bishop of Adria. 51. Caesar, whom Paul also mentions, became the bishop of Dyrrachium. 52. Mark, the cousin of Barnabas, whom Paul also mentions, became the bishop of Apollonia. 53. Joseph, who is also called Justus and Barsabbas, whom Luke mentions in the Acts of the Apostles as having been chosen along with Matthias, became the bishop of Eleutheropolis. 54. Artemas, whom Paul also mentions, became the bishop in Lystra. 55. Clement, whom Paul also mentions, saying: 'With Clement and the rest who were my fellow workers, who was the first among the Gentiles and Greeks to believe in Christ,' became the bishop of Sardis. 56. Onesiphorus, whom Paul also mentions, became the bishop of Coronea. 57. Tychicus, whom Paul also mentions, became the first bishop of Chalcedon in Bithynia. 58. english: He became [bishop] of Antioch along with Peter the leader. 6. Philemon, to whom Paul wrote a personal letter, became bishop of Gaza. 7. Zenas the lawyer, whom Paul also mentions, became bishop of Diospolis. 8. Aquila, whom Paul also mentions, became bishop of Heraclea. 9. Priscilla, whom Paul also mentions, became bishop of Colossae. 10. Junia, whom Paul also mentions, became bishop of Apamea of Syria. 126. Mark, also called John, whom Luke mentions in the Acts of the Apostles, became bishop of Byblos. 17. Aristarchus, whom Paul also mentions. 18. Pudens, whom Paul also mentions. 19. Trophimus, whom the apostle Paul also mentions. These three, having suffered all the persecutions of the apostle Paul along with him, were finally completed through martyrdom along with him, having their heads cut off by Nero. Counting Mark and Luke the evangelist with these, the number is 70. Under the holy Epiphanius, archbishop of Cyprus. These are the names of the 12 apostles.

1. Peter, who was also called Simon, Cephas, and Simeon. 2. Andrew, his brother. 3. James. 4. John, who were called Boanerges, which is interpreted as sons of thunder. 5. Philip. 6. Bartholomew. 7. Matthew the tax collector. 8. Thomas, who was also called Didymus. 9. James son of Alphaeus. 10. Thaddaeus, who is called Levi by Matthew, Judas son of James by Luke, and Leucius by Mark, sitting by the tax office. 11. Simon the Cananite. 12. Judas Iscariot, and in his place Matthias entered. The brothers Peter and Andrew, sons of Annas, and James and John, sons of Zebedee, and James and Judas, sons of Alphaeus, were fishermen. Peter and Andrew, James and John. James, who was called the brother of the Lord, who was the one who became bishop of Jerusalem and was nicknamed the Just; one was the son of Zebedee and the other of Alphaeus, and the other was the son of Joseph the betrothed, as the Jews said. Simon and Judas, Matthew calls them tax collectors, but Luke and Leucius are called tax collectors. Jonah is interpreted as dove.
